name: Jeddah
tagline: Gateway to Mecca, coral-stone old town and the Red Sea
summary: The Red Sea port where most pilgrims arrive, with a coral-stone old town of carved wooden balconies, a long corniche and some of the best reef diving in the region.
seasonNote: Humid and hot from May to October; winter is warm and pleasant.
arrival: King Abdulaziz International Airport is 20 km north; the Haramain train runs to Mecca and Medina.
gettingAround: Ride-hailing apps and taxis; Al-Balad is walkable.
cashTip: Cards everywhere; small cash for the souq.
foodTip: Hejazi food: ful medames for breakfast, mutabbaq, sayadiyah fish rice and Al Baik, which started here.
buyTip: Perfume, spices and textiles in Al-Balad's souqs.
baseArea: The North Corniche or near Al-Balad

items.name: Al-Balad historic district
items.summary: The old town of coral-stone tower houses with carved wooden rawasheen balconies and busy souqs.
items.expect: Some houses are under restoration; it comes alive after dark.
items.tip: Visit Nassif House, then walk the souqs in the evening.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.
items.sourceNote: Editorial selection. Durations, spending allowances and itinerary advice are planning estimates; check opening days and prices with the venue before you go.
whyVisit: The old town of coral-stone tower houses with carved wooden rawasheen balconies and busy souqs.
A UNESCO World Heritage site and the gateway pilgrims walked through for centuries.
visitFlow: Nassif House, Souq Al Alawi, then dinner in the lanes.
items.bestFor: Visitors interested in history and context and architecture and design
tradeoffs: Some houses are under restoration; it comes alive after dark.
